requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 167/167 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed
Receipts/GeneratedCodeExcludeFromCoverageTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (1/1), passes on head (1/1)
Receipts/GeneratedCodeExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTfmTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed

findings.claim: Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get generated formatters and resolvers with no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. Its derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0, and class targets are valid there. The guard therefore drops the attribute on targets that support it, which includes most multi-targeted libraries. Ledger L5 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedCodeExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTfmTests.GeneratedTypesAreExcludedOnLegacyTargets. It runs the generator with the NETSTANDARD2_0 and with the NETFRAMEWORK preprocessor symbol defined, then checks the generated formatter and resolver class declarations for the attribute. It fails on head because the attribute sits in an inactive #if region.

findings.claim: The generator now puts `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on its half of the user's `partial class` resolver (ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate). The attribute has AllowMultiple = false. A user who already marks their `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class X` with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (the obvious manual workaround before this change) now gets CS0579 'Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute', so existing projects stop compiling.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.UserResolverAlreadyExcludedFromCoverage_CompilesWithoutErrors. It runs MessagePackGenerator on a user partial resolver that already carries [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and asserts the output compilation has no errors. On head it reports CS0579; on base it compiles.

findings.claim: The guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is wider than it needs to be. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in every .NET Framework version MessagePack supports (4.0+), and it applies to classes there. Yet the attribute is dropped for every library targeting netstandard2.0 or net4x, which is a large share of consumers. So the requirement 'all generated code is decorated' is not met on those targets. Conditional emission was only justified where the attribute does not exist.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.FormattersExcludedFromCoverage_WhenNetStandard20SymbolDefined. It compiles with preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 against references that contain the attribute, then asserts every generated IMessagePackFormatter<T> implementation carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head the attribute is stripped.

hunches.claim: The attribute is emitted behind `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Users on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework (including the library's own netstandard2.0 targets) get no coverage exclusion, so the requirement 'all generated code' is only partly met. The ledger says to follow the requirement, so this is a scope gap.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter in a project targeting netstandard2.0 or net472 and check the output. Confirm the guarded attribute is compiled out and the type stays in coverage reports.

hunches.claim: The `#if` directives are emitted at column 0 inside generated nested-type bodies, and the TransformUtilities change adds a newline after `{` when constraints are present. This changes the layout of the generated output for every nested type with constraints. Users who check in or snapshot generator output will see diffs beyond the attribute. This is a behavior change outside the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests for nested generic types with constraints. Verify the diff in the snapshots comes only from the new attribute and not from whitespace or newline changes.

hunches.claim: The preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK are evaluated in the user's compilation, so the guard is inexact. A target such as netstandard2.1 or net462 has the attribute available, but others such as .NET Core 2.x or Unity may not. If the symbol set in a user project lacks the attribute, the generated code fails to compile. This is a breaking compile error for existing users who upgrade the generator.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the generated output in a project targeting netstandard2.1, net6.0, and Unity-style older frameworks that lack ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. Check for CS0234 or CS0246 errors.

hunches.claim: The nesting-type emission in TransformUtilities was changed from `{` to `{\r\n` when constraints exist. This is a behavior change outside the attribute requirement, probably needed so the following `#if` starts on its own line. It affects all generated nested-type output, and nothing in the ledger covers it.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests and confirm that only whitespace changes in the nested generic-constrained type snapshots.

hunches.claim: The diff has no hand-written test hunks. The only verification is the 222 regenerated snapshots. Snapshot tests only prove the emitted text matches the committed text. They never compile the output under netstandard2.0/.NETFRAMEWORK versus modern TFMs, so the `#if` guard is not exercised.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/FormatterTemplate.cs:33 negate-condition: `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` -> `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK`; expected to survive unless the snapshots are regenerated, because no test compiles the generated code under different TFMs and asserts the attribute is present or absent.

hunches.claim: The `.tt` templates and the hand-edited `.cs` outputs are changed separately. No test checks that they agree, so they can drift (e.g. missed attribute on one type). Snapshot tests only cover the `.cs` output and only the types the snapshot inputs happen to exercise. The CompositeResolver template and nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper classes may have no snapshot coverage.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/CompositeResolverTemplate.cs:27 delete-statement: remove the `#if ... ExcludeFromCodeCoverage ... #endif` text from the Write string; expected to survive if no CompositeResolver snapshot test exists.

hunches.claim:
The TransformUtilities change from `{` to `{
` for constrained nesting types changes generated whitespace. It is needed so the `#if` directive lands on its own line after the brace. No dedicated test covers a nested generic type with constraints. A revert would only break snapshots if such an input exists.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/TransformUtilities.cs:58 swap-boolean: `anyConstraints ? "{\r\n" : ...` -> `anyConstraints ? "{" : ...`; expected to survive unless a snapshot has a nested type with generic constraints followed by a formatter, and without the newline `{#if` would break compilation.

hunches.claim: The README says the attribute is not available for `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework. That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in both. The docs therefore misstate why coverage exclusion is missing on those targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a netstandard2.0 class library and a net472 class library, each with `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] class C {}`. Both build, which contradicts README.md:1640.

hunches.claim: Attribute is emitted only under `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so generated code on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework is not excluded from coverage. The requirement says all generated code. Ledger L5 answered 'No preference; follow the requirement', so this gap is not recorded as deliberate. The conditional emission is permitted by the requirement's derived criterion (attribute must exist or be conditionally emitted).

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guards in the templates with acceptance criterion 1 (all generated code decorated). L5 gives no recorded decision to exclude those targets.

hunches.claim: The README sentence documents the decision to skip netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, which is a user-visible limitation. Nothing in the ledger records it as an intended product behavior.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the README addition against the ledger. L5 is the only related entry and it expresses no preference.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute unconditionally, with no setting. Every generated formatter (int-key, string-key, enum, union) and every resolver, including its nested FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper types, gets `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` behind a target-framework `#if`. Users cannot turn it off.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Same decoration, but with an opt-out setting as the requirement permits. Add a boolean option to GeneratorOptions, e.g. `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, defaulting to true and readable from the generator's existing options source (assembly attribute or analyzer config). Pass it to the templates. In each .tt/.cs template, write the `#if`/attribute lines only when the option is true. Add snapshot tests covering both settings and a README note describing the option.
